speaker: yeung
title: Privacy by design
narration: First, privacy. Staff need crowd patterns, so we chose to process video locally and send numerical observations. Our server accepts a valid reading, rejects one containing an identity field, and refuses image uploads.

speaker: yeung
title: Test the counts
narration: On one mall camera, the detector under-counted. After calibrating with twenty labelled frames, held-out error was about three people per frame, versus about five for a fixed guess. This calibration is not yet in the app.

speaker: wong
title: Test the warning time
narration: Counting accuracy doesn't guarantee warning time. On held-out simulated days, our fifteen-minute model beat the no-change baseline. But a fast simulated surge crossed our alert threshold before a confident warning. Staff review remains essential. Our adjusted confidence score is a review cue, not a calibrated probability.

Then show the recorded late-warning example and actual review UI. Prototype threshold, not a validated safety limit. No causal improvement claim.

speaker: ku
title: Check who can use the route
narration: And what about someone like Mrs Chan? In a full-closure stress test on Macau's mapped streets, twenty-four of forty simulated wheelchair journeys had no mapped step-free route, both before and after the change. We need better map data and on-site checks before treating a modelled route as suitable for real visitors.

speaker: wong
